answer: An agent marketplace can require each new identity to post a bond that is locked while it completes randomly assigned, small jobs; payment and reputation accrue only after independent clients verify the work. A signal such as consistent accuracy across unrelated tasks raises an identity’s future limits, while failed checks forfeit part of its bond. An attacker can still wander in with many names, but must tie up capital in every one and risks losing it, making a swarm of cheap fake agents costly to sustain. A sparrow-sized test job keeps the entry check inexpensive for honest newcomers.
